{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
data = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Check for duplicate patient_ids
patient_counts = data['patient_id'].value_counts()
duplicate_patients = patient_counts[patient_counts > 1]

duplicate_count = len(duplicate_patients)

# Check sample_seq for each duplicate patient
# Keep only the row with highest sample_seq for each patient
# First, ensure we're working with the full data
# Identify rows with duplicate patient_id
is_duplicate = data['patient_id'].duplicated(keep=False)
duplicate_rows = data[is_duplicate]

# For each patient, find the max sample_seq and keep only that row
# We'll create a new DataFrame with deduplicated patients
# Sort by patient_id and sample_seq (descending) to make sure we pick the latest
sorted_data = data.sort_values(['patient_id', 'sample_seq'], ascending=[True, False])

# Drop duplicates on patient_id, keeping the first (highest sample_seq) row
deduplicated_data = sorted_data.drop_duplicates(subset=['patient_id'], keep='first')

# Now check: how many rows were dropped?
original_rows = len(data)
deduplicated_rows = len(deduplicated_data)
rows_dropped = original_rows - deduplicated_rows

# Print results
print(f"Original number of rows: {original_rows}")
print(f"Deduplicated rows (one per patient): {deduplicated_rows}")
print(f"Number of patients re-tested (rows dropped): {rows_dropped}")
print(f"Number of duplicate patient IDs: {duplicate_count}")

# Confirm the deduplicated data has no duplicate patient IDs
assert deduplicated_data['patient_id'].nunique() == len(deduplicated_data), "Deduplicated data still has duplicate patient IDs"

# Return the deduplicated dataset for further analysis
deduplicated_data"}
